attempts.hypothesis: AC-1: displayProgram computes the first token exactly as the claim states (ASCII-whitespace-delimited)
attempts.method: Compared the claim's rule with the implementation for a token preceded by U+00A0 and for a token carrying an internal U+200B
attempts.evidence: displayProgram(['\u00A0docker']) returns 'docker'. U+00A0 is not ASCII whitespace, so the rule as stated ('the first ASCII-whitespace-delimited token of argv[0]' = '\u00A0docker', which fails the regex) would render '(no command)'; the implementation's .trim() is Unicode-aware and strips it first. The divergence renders more, not less, and the output is still only [A-Za-z0-9._+-]{1,64}, so there is no credential consequence - hence nit, not major

findings.message: The d109ae1 renderer replacement left three documentation-of-record sites describing the OLD behaviour, so the code's own account of a security-relevant rendering contradicts the code. src/policy.ts:158 documents displayProgram as 'basename of argv[0], redacted with the audit rules (a program name CAN be credential-shaped - argv[0]="Authorization: Bearer sk-live-..." was reproduced by adversarial review), capped so a pathological argument cannot flood the operator channel'; src/host-runner.ts:65 documents it as '(basename, redacted, capped, never blank)'; extensions/index.ts:150 documents the one-shot notice as 'already redacted' (and its onFirstHostRun comment as 'an already REDACTED rendering'). The implementation does none of these: it takes the first whitespace-delimited token and whitelists ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._+-]{0,63}$, with no basename step and no redaction - the quoted 'Authorization: Bearer sk-live-...' example now renders '(no command)'. No runtime effect and the published docs (docs/security.md, CHANGELOG) are correct, but a maintainer reading these comments would believe an audit redaction rule is still in the path.

The new reverse guard makes every devcontainer_exec perform a SECOND full workspace discovery. In src/execution-service.ts a container-exec now calls options.mappingFor(ctx.workspaceKey) (the new guard, line ~190) and later options.resolveContainerWorkspace(ctx.workspaceKey) (the pre-existing presentation path, line ~288); in extensions/index.ts both are wired to functions that await the uncached registry(), which runs a host filesystem traversal plus 'docker ps --all --no-trunc' on every call (registry() has no memo), and readMapping is a near line-for-line duplicate of resolveContainerWorkspace. I confirmed with the real ExecutionService that one container-exec invokes both hooks exactly once each, so the change doubles a subprocess-spawning discovery per devcontainer_exec compared with the merge base (which performed one). It remains read-only and bounded, so AC-6 is not falsified, but the codebase elsewhere explicitly avoids discovering twice for one command and the two resolvers should share one read.

AC-4's 'binds exactly the picked candidate' fails when two candidates render the same picker label. chooseAmbiguousContainer builds labels as '<id.slice(0,12)> - <state>[ - <image>]' and maps the operator's answer back with labels.indexOf(picked), so two candidates whose ids share their first 12 characters (and whose state and image match) produce identical labels; the second row can never be bound. Confirmed by driving the real use handler: with candidates aaaaaaaaaaaa1111... and aaaaaaaaaaaa2222... (both running, same image), picking the second identical row bound candidate[0] and echoed 'Selected `/ws/project-a` -> container `aaaaaaaaaaaa1111...`'. It needs a 48-bit id-prefix collision, hence nit, but mapping a selection through a display string instead of the picker's index is the fragile part.

The published rendering contract omits the length bound the code enforces. docs/security.md ('a single word of [A-Za-z0-9._+-] starting with an alphanumeric') and the CHANGELOG bullet ('a single program word ([A-Za-z0-9._+-], leading alphanumeric)') state no cap, but the implementation's regex is ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._+-]{0,63}$, so displayProgram(['a'.repeat(65)]) renders '(no command)' and displayProgram(['a'.repeat(64)]) renders the word. Grepping docs, CHANGELOG and both READMEs finds the 64 ceiling nowhere, so the published specification claims a rendering the code refuses for a program-name-shaped token; AC-1 itself states the bound, so only the published docs are imprecise.

AC-1's stated tokenization is not what the implementation performs. The claim says displayProgram 'takes the first ASCII-whitespace-delimited token of argv[0]', but the implementation trims first with String.prototype.trim (Unicode-aware) and only then splits on [ \t\n\r\f\v]. Observed: displayProgram(['\u00A0docker']) returns 'docker', whereas dragging the AC's ASCII-whitespace rule over the raw argv[0] ('\u00A0docker' is one token, which fails the regex) yields '(no command)'. The divergence renders a program word the AC says would not render; it cannot expose anything outside [A-Za-z0-9._+-]{1,64}, so it is a specification/implementation mismatch rather than a leak.
